_comment: DATA-DRIVEN runner disk-reclaim policy (FRIC-017 productization, pipeline-glue(b), ADR-0548 pipeline-as-product). The Rust-first preflight binary oya-cloud-ci-runner-disk-reclaim reads this file and, for the requested runner profile, best-effort removes the listed vendor preinstall dirs BEFORE the multi-GB buck-out warm restore, then ASSERTS the post-reclaim free-disk floor. Replaces the two duplicated inline `sudo rm -rf` blocks in .github/workflows/oya-ci-required.yml (the buck2 + gate-affected-set jobs) per the founder doctrine 'new automation never ships as shell'. Each profile names the reclaim_dirs (best-effort, like the old `|| true`) + min_free_gib_after (the post-reclaim floor; below it the preflight emits a distinct INFRA-RED signal so a downstream disk-exhaustion is attributable to INFRA, not CODE). The dirs are vendor preinstall trees that no oya/buck2 action consumes; removing them touches NO repo content and NO cache (buck-out / ~/.rustup / the restored blob), so the ADR-0556/0560 cold==warm integrity canary is unaffected.

github-hosted-ubuntu-latest._comment: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest carries ~25-30 GiB of .NET/Android/GHC/CodeQL vendor preinstall on a runner with only ~14 GiB free on /. The buck-out warm restore decompresses a ~5.78 GiB blob (~12-15 GiB on disk) on top of a fetch-depth:0 monorepo checkout, exhausting / (FRIC-017: 'No space left on device' at restore, before any build ran). The 5 dirs are the vendor preinstall trees removed by the retired inline shell.

owned-arc-arm64._comment: Owned ARC container runner (ADR-0515 D5 owned-runner readiness). ARCH IS SCALE-SET METADATA, NOT ENGINE LOGIC: the profile id names the AutoscalingRunnerSet (`oya-arm64` in ns arc-runners, whose pod template pins nodeSelector kubernetes.io/arch=arm64); an amd64 scale set adds a SIBLING DATA ROW here with zero code change — the preflight has no arch branch. reclaim_dirs is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION: the ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner image carries none of the GitHub vendor preinstall trees (dotnet/android/ghc/ghcup/CodeQL), so there is nothing to reclaim and copying the github-hosted list here would be a no-op that lies about what the preflight did. THE FLOOR IS MEASURED AGAINST THE POD'S DECLARED EPHEMERAL-STORAGE, NOT GUESSED: statvfs inside a container runner reports the NODE's shared filesystem, so the only defensible floor is the per-runner ephemeral-storage budget the fleet can actually honor — measured 2026-07-29: node allocatable ephemeral-storage 45909593217 B (42 GiB, uniform across the 3 Talos nodes) / maxRunners 3 = 14 GiB per runner. 3 x 14 GiB = 42 GiB fits one node in the worst case where all runners co-schedule (the pod template declares no anti-affinity). Below the floor the node cannot honor the declaration and the preflight emits INFRA-RED, which is correct: it is a capacity fact, not a code failure. THE GITHUB-HOSTED 20 GiB FLOOR IS WRONG HERE and asserting it against this fleet INFRA-REDs every job. INERT UNTIL PAIRED: this profile has no consumer until the runner pod template declares matching `resources.requests/limits.ephemeral-storage: 14Gi` (it declares NONE today, so the pod is guaranteed nothing) and a job is actually routed to the owned scale set. The conformance gate pins floor <= allocatable/maxRunners so a copy-paste of the github-hosted number REDs.
